hints: Focus on what those two IR regions tell you, the 1670 to 1740 region is the C=O stretch and the broad 2500 to 3000 region is the O-H of a carboxylic acid.
Check S first, it has no C=O absorption, so rule out any S structure that already contains a ketone, aldehyde, acid or ester group.
Check T next, it must have a C=O but must not be a carboxylic acid, then ask which S to T change fits cleavage of an alkene by hot, concentrated KMnO4.
walkthrough:
**Decode the IR data for S**

S shows no strong absorption between 1670 and 1740 cm-1. That is the key region for $C=O$ stretching.

Rule: $C=O$ (ketone, aldehyde, carboxylic acid, ester) absorbs strongly around $1680$ to $1750$ cm-1. So S contains no $C=O$ group.

**Decode the IR data for T**

T has a strong absorption at 1720 cm-1, so T does contain $C=O$.

But T has no strong, broad absorption between 2500 and 3000 cm-1. That broad band is the $O-H$ stretch of a carboxylic acid, $RCO_2H$.

Conclusion: T is a carbonyl compound but not a carboxylic acid. It is most likely a ketone, aldehyde or ester.

**Link to hot, concentrated KMnO4 chemistry**

Hot, concentrated $KMnO_4$ is a very vigorous oxidant. It cleaves $C=C$ double bonds completely.

A cyclic alkene can be ring-opened to give two new $C=O$ groups. If both ends are alkyl substituted, you get a diketone, with no acid formed.

This fits perfectly: S (alkene, no C=O) to T (diketone, C=O but no acid O-H).

**Apply to the options**

Option B has S as a substituted cyclohexene with only C-C and C-H bonds and C=C, so no 1670 to 1740 band. Its T is $CH_3COCH_2CH_2COCH(CH_3)_2$, a diketone with strong C=O at 1720 cm-1 and no acid O-H. That matches both IR descriptions and the oxidative ring-opening.

options.A: S as $CH_3(CH_2)_5CH=CH_2$ fits S with no C=O, but T as $CH_3(CH_2)_5CO_2H$ is a carboxylic acid. It would show both C=O near 1720 cm-1 and a strong, broad O-H band from 2500 to 3000 cm-1, which T is said not to have.
options.B: S is a methyl(isopropyl)cyclohexene, an alkene with no C=O, so no 1670 to 1740 cm-1 band. Hot, concentrated KMnO4 cleaves and ring-opens the C=C to give the diketone $CH_3COCH_2CH_2COCH(CH_3)_2$. This T has C=O absorption at 1720 cm-1 but no carboxylic acid O-H, exactly as described. Lovely match.
options.C: S already contains a $CH_3CO-$ ketone group attached to the ring. A ketone gives a strong C=O absorption between 1670 and 1740 cm-1, so S would absorb there. This directly contradicts the statement that S has no absorption in that region.
options.D: S as a diene hydrocarbon fits S with no C=O, but T as $HO_2CCH_2CH_2COCH_2COCH_3$ contains a $CO_2H$ group. It would show the broad 2500 to 3000 cm-1 O-H absorption of a carboxylic acid, which T is said not to have.
